title: gut-notes-and-hypotheses-ira-cooper
content:
Candidate: Ira Cooper
Role: Senior Inference Engineer (runtime-focused)
Context: 60-minute loop (system design + code walkthrough + behavioral). I wrote these in real-time and then expanded them after thinking for a couple hours. Not polished — meant to capture instincts and hypotheses to help decide whether to re-loop.

Quick take (first instincts)
- Very strong systems intuition around memory/latency trade-offs. Talks about KV cache and attention cache like it’s plumbing — good sign for runtime ops.
- Slightly weak on empirical validation: loves mental models but had trouble naming specific metrics he'd collect for a production rollout (e.g., P95 token latencies broken down by sequence length, cache hit distribution).
- Communication: clear, concise. Asks good clarifying Qs, but pauses to reframe frequently (could be thinking aloud — fine).

Signal: architecture and tradeoffs (positive)
- When asked about handling mixed seq-length traffic he laid out a sensible routing strategy: short requests to a low-latency pool; long requests to batch-optimized backends with async streaming. Mentioned prefix caching and dynamic batching thresholds.
- Brought up kernel-level optimization choices (FP16 vs 8-bit quantization tradeoffs) and pragmatic rollout approach (start with quantized variant in canary for non-critical tenants).
- Suggests using a lightweight admission controller that uses request-cost estimate (tokens * model_cost) to gate batch assignment — aligns with our cost-aware routing thesis.

Red flags / things to probe
- When pressed on observability, initial answers were vague. Eventually proposed event types but couldn't name concrete SLI values for an SLO (e.g., acceptable P99 generation time for 1–64 token queries).
- Light on orchestration failure modes: didn't proactively call out KV cache invalidation scenarios or model rollback hazards related to stateful session affinity.
- Limited experience with GPU memory fragmentation at scale — has read about it but not owned a large-scale mitigation project.

Behavioral / culture fit notes
- Pragmatic but not dogmatic. Prefers principle-driven decisions and values measurability.
- Comfortable with cross-team tradeoffs (infra <> product). Gave an example of prioritizing a production outage postmortem over shipping a small perf gain.
- Seems like a builder who cares about developer ergonomics (mentioned last role building internal SDK for easier model rollouts).

Hypotheses to validate on a re-loop
- Will perform well on a short pairing task focused on observability: give him a small service that logs token latencies and ask him to propose a dashboard and a set of alerts with concrete thresholds. His verbal answers were thin here; a hands-on exercise should reveal depth.
- If asked to design a rollout that includes quantized model variant with automated fallbacks for quality regressions, I expect he can produce a safe plan (canary config, automatic fallback criteria based on eval set mismatch), but might skip some edge-cases unless prompted.

Suggested technical probe list (for loop 2)
- Pairing task: add a metric and an alert to a toy inference endpoint; show the concrete queries that trigger the alert and how you'd troubleshoot.
- System design mini: design routing policy for 3 model variants (fast-small, balanced, high-quality) across two regions with capacity constraints and SLA tiers. Focus on cost/latency tradeoffs and automatic fallback.
- Short whiteboard: memory layout for KV cache and how you'd instrument cache evictions and fragmentation detection.

Scorecard (quick, not final)
- System design: 4/5 (good tradeoffs, practical routing ideas)
- Debugging/observability: 3/5 (conceptual ok, lacks concrete metrics)
- Production ownership: 4/5 (clear examples, cares about ops)
- Communication: 4/5 (clear, asks clarifying Qs)
- Overall hire inclination: lean-hire pending pairing exercise.

Suggested decision path
- Move to a 60–90 minute pairing loop focused on observability and a small code exercise. Bring one infra engineer (Aisha) to watch for memory-level specifics and one PM/PMM to probe tradeoffs in latency vs cost.
- If pairing shows ability to define concrete SLIs and to propose workable remediation steps for observability gaps, greenlight. Otherwise, decline.

Misc notes and idiosyncratic impressions
- Mentions previous employer where they reduced per-token cost by ~20% via smarter batch sizing and caching. Could ask for an artifact or metric to validate the claim.
- Appreciates ergonomic SDKs; asked about our client libraries and whether teams can opt into auto-batching. Good candidate for a role that interfaces with product and platform teams.
- Appears level-headed under hypothetical outage pressure. Answered an outage scenario slowly but with a sensible escalation path (fewer changes, switch traffic to standby, analyze live sampling).

Write-ups to attach for loop 2 prep
- Small repo with an express endpoint that emits token timing and a basic Prometheus export (link in linked_artifacts).
- Two short prompts for canary/rollback exercise (quality-check harness).
- One pager: our standard pairing rubric focusing on observability and memory.

Immediate action: schedule pairing with candidate and loop participants Aisha + Diego.

Open questions for myself before re-loop
- How comfortable am I with the knowledge gap on GPU fragmentation? Could it be covered by mentoring from current team members?
- Do we need someone with deep fragmentation/driver experience, or is strong systems intuition + ownership sufficient?

End of notes.

(voice: quick, stream-of-consciousness. Not for external sharing yet.)
